title: विद्यार्थी सिकाइ उपलब्धि: असमानताका आयामहरू र कक्षाकोठामा आधारित परीक्षा (Student Learning Achievement: Dimensions of Inequalities and Classroom-based Examination)
nepali: औपचारिक शिक्षा प्रणालीमा राष्ट्रिय पाठ्यक्रमले निर्धारण गरेका सिकाइ उपलब्धि हासिल गराउनका लागि विभिन्न प्रक्रिया, संरचना र क्रियाकलापहरू निर्धारण गरिएको हुन्छ । सोही अनुसार संरचित पाठ्यक्रम, पाठ्यपुस्तक, शिक्षक निर्देशिका, पाठ्यक्रम प्रवोधिकरण, अन्य शैक्षिक सामग्री, निश्चित योग्यता र क्षमता भएका शिक्षक, प्रधानाध्यापक, व्यवस्थापन समिति, विद्यालयको भौतिक पक्ष लगायत अन्य प्रशासनिक इकाइहरूको व्यवस्था गरिएको हुन्छ । यी सबै व्यवस्थाहरू विद्यार्थीमा तोकिएको सिकाइ उपलब्धि अधिकतम रूपमा हासिल गराउनेतर्फ लक्षित हुन्छन् । शैक्षिक सुशासन र जवाफदेहितालाई प्रवर्धन गर्दै विद्यार्थीको सिकाइ उपलब्धि हासिल गराउनु मुख्य उद्देश्य भएकाले त्यसको परीक्षण गर्ने कार्यलाई पनि अझ महत्वपूर्ण मानिन्छ । परीक्षामा आधारित जवाफदेहिताका अभ्यासहरू प्रचलित छन् । नेपालमा कक्षा ३, ५, ८ र १० मा राष्ट्रिय उपलब्धि परीक्षण र कक्षा ८, १० र १२ मा सार्वजनिक परीक्षा हुने गरेको छ । यी परीक्षाहरूका नतिजाले विद्यार्थीको सिकाइ उपलब्धि निरन्तर कमजोर हुँदै गएको र त्यो कमजोर सिकाइ उपलब्धिमा पनि विभिन्न खाले गहिरा असमानताहरू देखाएका छन् । यो लेख सिकाइ उपलब्धिमा देखिएका विभिन्नखाले असमानता आयामहरू कस्ता छन्, कुन कुन समूहका बीच के कति मात्रामा असमानता छ र ती असमानता कम गर्न कक्षाकोठामा आधारित परीक्षाले कसरी सहयोग गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्नहरूमा आधारित छ। द्वितीय स्रोतबाट प्राप्त परिमाणात्मक तथ्याङ्क र अनुसन्धानकर्ताले सङ्कलन गरेका प्राथमिक गुणात्मक सूचना र विभिन्न अध्ययन अनुसन्धानलाई सन्दर्भ सामग्रीको रूपमा प्रयोग गरी ती असमानताहरूलाई विश्लेषण गरिएको छ । सिकाइ उपलब्धिमा विभिन्नखाले असमानताहरू विद्यमान रहेका छन् । ती असमानताहरूलाई न्यूनीकरण गर्न कक्षाकोठामा आधारित परीक्षालाई प्रभावकारी बनाउन आवश्यक छ । यसका लागि शिक्षक क्षमता विकास र परीक्षाका अभ्यासका लागि विद्यालयको स्वायत्तामा जोड दिनु आवश्यक हुन्छ ।
american_english: In the formal education system, a range of processes, structures and activities are laid down in order to secure the learning outcomes prescribed by the national curriculum. In line with that, provision is made for a structured curriculum, textbooks, teacher's guides, curriculum handbooks, other instructional materials, teachers with defined qualifications and competencies, principals, management committees, the school's physical facilities and other administrative units. All of these arrangements are aimed at getting students to attain the prescribed learning outcomes to the maximum degree. Since the main objective is to raise student learning outcomes while promoting educational governance and accountability, the task of testing them is considered all the more important. Examination-based accountability practices are in place. In Nepal, national achievement tests are administered in grades 3, 5, 8 and 10, and public examinations in grades 8, 10 and 12. The results of these examinations show that students' learning outcomes have been getting steadily weaker and that this weak performance itself reveals various kinds of deep inequality. This article is built around the questions of what the different dimensions of inequality seen in learning outcomes are, between which groups and to what extent inequality exists, and how classroom-based testing helps reduce those inequalities. The inequalities have been analyzed using quantitative data obtained from secondary sources, primary qualitative information collected by the researcher, and various studies and research as reference material. Different kinds of inequality persist in learning outcomes. Classroom-based testing needs to be made effective in order to reduce those inequalities. To that end, it is necessary to place emphasis on teacher capacity building and on school autonomy for examination practices.
british_english: Within the formal education system, various processes, structures and activities are prescribed in order to secure the learning attainments laid down by the national curriculum. Accordingly, provision is made for a structured curriculum, textbooks, teachers' guides, curriculum handbooks, other teaching materials, teachers holding specified qualifications and competencies, headteachers, management committees, the school's physical fabric and other administrative units. All these arrangements are directed at enabling pupils to attain the prescribed learning attainment to the greatest possible extent. As the principal aim is to secure pupils' learning attainment while advancing educational governance and accountability, the business of assessing it is likewise regarded as all the more important. Practices of accountability founded on examinations are well established. In Nepal, national achievement tests are conducted in classes 3, 5, 8 and 10, and public examinations in classes 8, 10 and 12. The results of these examinations have shown that pupils' learning attainment has been declining steadily and that even that weak attainment exhibits deep inequalities of various kinds. The present article is founded on the questions of what the various dimensions of inequality observed in learning attainment are, between which groups and in what measure inequality obtains, and how classroom-based examination assists in lessening those inequalities. Those inequalities have been analysed by drawing on quantitative data obtained from secondary sources, primary qualitative information gathered by the researcher, and various studies and research as reference material. Inequalities of various kinds exist in learning attainment. Classroom-based examination needs to be made effective if those inequalities are to be reduced. For this purpose it is necessary to place weight on teacher capacity development and on schools' autonomy in respect of examination practice.
australian_english: In the formal education system, a mix of processes, structures and activities is set down to achieve the learning achievements laid out by the national curriculum. In keeping with that, arrangements are made for a structured curriculum, textbooks, teacher's guides, curriculum handbooks, other teaching materials, teachers with the required qualifications and capacities, principals, management committees, the school's physical side and other administrative units. All of these arrangements are aimed at getting students to reach the prescribed learning achievement to the fullest extent. Given that the main aim is to lift students' learning achievement while promoting educational governance and accountability, the job of testing it is seen as all the more important too. Examination-based accountability practices are commonplace. In Nepal, national achievement testing takes place in classes 3, 5, 8 and 10, and public examinations in classes 8, 10 and 12. The results of these examinations show that students' learning achievement has been slipping steadily and that even that weak achievement turns up various kinds of deep inequality. This article hangs on the questions of what sorts of inequality dimensions show up in learning achievement, which groups sit on either side of the gap and by how much, and how classroom-based examination helps close that gap. The inequalities have been analysed using quantitative data drawn from secondary sources, primary qualitative information the researcher collected, and various studies and research as reference material. Various kinds of inequality are present in learning achievement. Classroom-based examination needs to be made more effective to bring those inequalities down. For that, it is necessary to put weight on teacher capacity development and on schools having autonomy over their examination practices.
informal_english: In the formal school system, all sorts of processes, structures and activities get set up to make sure kids hit the learning achievements the national curriculum lays out. Alongside that, you have the structured curriculum, textbooks, teacher's guides, curriculum handbooks, other teaching gear, teachers with the right qualifications and skills, principals, management committees, the school's physical side and the other admin units all sorted. All of that is aimed at getting students to the prescribed learning achievement as far as it can go. Seeing as the main aim is to lift students' learning achievement while pushing educational governance and accountability, the job of testing it gets treated as even more important. Exams-based accountability is pretty standard. In Nepal, national achievement tests run in classes 3, 5, 8 and 10, and public exams in classes 8, 10 and 12. The results of these exams show that students' learning achievement has been getting weaker and weaker, and even that weak achievement has all sorts of deep inequalities in it. This article is built on a few questions: what do the different inequality dimensions in learning achievement actually look like, which groups are on which side of the gap and by how much, and how does classroom-based assessment help close that gap? The inequalities have been analysed using quantitative data from secondary sources, primary qualitative info the researcher gathered, and various studies and research as reference material. All sorts of inequalities are there in learning achievement. Classroom-based assessment needs to be made to work properly if those inequalities are going to come down. For that, you need to put the emphasis on teacher capacity building and on schools having a say over their own exam practices.
translator_notes: Twelve sentences in the source; order preserved across all variants. 'पाठ्यक्रम प्रवोधिकरण' is likely an OCR/typesetting corruption of a curriculum document term; rendered as curriculum handbooks (the standard Nepali curriculum-support publication). 'कक्षा ३/५/८/१०/१२' rendered as grades (US) and classes (UK/AU/NZ). Informal flavour: New Zealand casual.
